ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
title: NATIONAL APPRENTICESHIP PROMOTION AND TRAINING SCHEMES
content:
Press Release:Press Information Bureau Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship NATIONAL APPRENTICESHIP PROMOTION AND TRAINING SCHEMES Posted On:
                11 FEB 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India, under the Apprentices Act, 1961, implements two flagship Central Sector schemes namely National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), launched in August 2016 and continued as NAPS-2 from 2022-23 by Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) launched in 1973 by the Ministry of Education (MoE) and approved for its continuation up to 2025-26. Together these schemes, support apprenticeship engagement in the country. In the calendar year 2025, apprentices engaged under NAPS and NATS are 11.84 lakh and5.23 lakhrespectively. In both the schemes, apprenticeship participation is significantly strongin industries falling under top 13 sectors namelyAutomotive, Banking, Financial Services & Insurance (BFSI), Electrical (including New and Renewable Energy), Electronics, IT/ITeS, Life Sciences, Logistic and Supply Chain,Production and Manufacturing, Retail,Rubber, Service sectors (Education, Health Care, Professional services) and Tourism &Hospitality. Role of MSMEs under Apprenticeship training is to provide on-the job training to apprentices. Establishments including MSMEs that have engaged apprentices are 25,423 and 16,400 under NAPS-2 and NATS respectively. Both NAPS and NATS support apprenticeship engagement across the country by providing partial stipend support through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly to the apprentices engaged under the Apprentice Act, 1961. The Government share of stipend providedto apprentices under NAPS is limited to 25% of prescribed minimum stipend (up to a maximum of Rs.1,500 per month, per apprentice) and under NATS is limited to 50% of the prescribed minimum stipend (up to Rs.4,500 per month per apprentice).The Government recognises the successfully completed apprentices by issuing nationally recognised National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) under Designated trades of NAPS, Certificate of Proficiency (CoP) for Optional trades of NAPS and NATS. In addition, the government has issued lettersconsidering the training period undergone by an apprentice as an experience under both NAPS (for ITI graduates) and NATS.All these efforts support completion outcomes and aretranslating apprenticeship training to employment. The third-party evaluation reports from AJNIFM (Arun Jaitley National Institute of Finance Management) on NAPS and NILERD (National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development) on NATS indicates apprentices being engaged in a full time employment on completion of their training at 72 % and 74% respectively.Further, the 38th meeting of the CAC (Central Apprenticeship Council) held on 26 th May 2025, marked a significant advancement in modernizing the country’s apprenticeship framework. Key decisions included a 36% increase in apprentice stipends, with future revisions linked to the Consumer Price Index (CPI). This acts as an impetus for apprentices to complete the training. The Council in the above meeting also approved the introduction of Apprenticeship Embedded Degree/ Diploma programme (AEDP) under the ambit of the Act encouraging degree apprenticeships and promoting flexible delivery modes such as online and blended learning, and enabling apprentices to train at client locations within India and even abroad. Further, inclusive measures—such as dedicated provisions for persons with benchmark disabilities—were introduced. If the prescribed training places for fresher apprentice and skill certificate holder apprentice cannot be filled, then the establishments may fill the same with other categories of apprentices. The scope of apprenticeship training was also expanded to include emerging sectors under the NIC-2008 classification (e.g., IT, biotechnology, and renewable energy). In addition, the Council recommended the establishment of new regional apprenticeship boards beyond the existing ones in Chennai, Kanpur, Kolkata, and Mumbai. These decisions, made in consultation with the CAC, have been duly approved by the Hon’ble Minister and notified through Gazette of India.Further, under the Jan Vishwas 2.0 Bill, currently under examination by a Select Committee of Parliament, the Apprentices Act is proposed to be aligned towards  ease of doing business, compliance-oriented framework, with enforcement envisaged primarily through civil penalties and structured processes, consistent with the stated policy direction of decriminalisation while retaining statutory accountability.Under NAPS,to promote apprenticeship engagement in North-Eastern Region (NER),a focused pilot initiative was launched on 20.05.2025, that facilitates an additional incentive upto ₹1,500 per month to NER candidates undergoing Apprenticeship in any other state other than their domiciled State.This is over and above the government share of stipend upto ₹1,500 under NAPS. This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Shri Jayant Chaudhary in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. *** SH (Release ID: 2226495) Visitor Counter : 40 Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship NATIONAL APPRENTICESHIP PROMOTION AND TRAINING SCHEMES Posted On:

title: National Statistical Systems Training Academy, MoSPI to Celebrate 18th Foundation Day on 13th February 2026
content:
Press Release:Press Information Bureau Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation National Statistical Systems Training Academy, MoSPI to Celebrate 18th Foundation Day on 13th February 2026 Theme: Reimagining Capacity Building for Official Statistics to achieve vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 Posted On:
                11 FEB 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi The National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA), established on 13 February 2009 under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), will celebrate its 18th Foundation Day on 13 February 2026 at Greater Noida. NSSTA is a Central Training Institute under Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation established for fostering human resource development in Official Statistics and related disciplines. NSSTA plays a key role in strengthening statistical capacity by providing high-quality training to the officers of the Central and State/UT Government, as well as repositioning itself internationally by conducting training for international participants. The occasion marks eighteen years of the Academy’s dedicated contribution to strengthening India’s statistical systems and promoting evidence-based governance through sustained capacity building. Marking its Foundation Day, NSSTA will celebrate this year under the theme “Reimagining Capacity Building for Official Statistics to achieve the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047,” underscoring the critical role of strong, reliable, and future-ready statistical systems in India’s developmental journey. As the country advances toward becoming a developed nation by 2047, the focus has expanded beyond data collection to building institutional capacities, adopting cutting-edge technologies like AI/ML, big data analytics, Harmonization of data to make it AI ready and nurturing skilled human resources. As the nation’s premier training institute for official statistics and related disciplines, NSSTA continues to lead these efforts by equipping statistical professionals with modern methodologies and fostering a culture of continuous learning and innovation. The celebration will bring together policymakers, experts, and practitioners to deliberate on reimagining capacity building to strengthening evidence-based governance and enhancing effective communications. The Foundation Day ceremony will be graced by the presence of Rao Inderjit Singh, Hon’ble MOS (I/C), M/o S&PI, MOS (I/C), M/o Planning and MOS, M/o Culture, and other distinguished dignitaries, including Ms. S. Radha Chauhan, IAS, Chairperson, Capacity Building Commission (CBC); Dr. Saurabh Garg, IAS, Secretary, MoSPI; Mr. Stefan Priesner, UN Resident Coordinator in India, Director Generals and other senior officers. The high-level Plenary Session will provide key insights and further directions for strengthening capacity building and deeper collaborations with various stakeholders. Following the plenary, the event will transition into a dynamic Panel Discussion on very important contemporary topic namely “Communicating statistics to the policymakers and public” by the eminent personalities. The event is expected to bring together over 350 participants, including senior officers of Centre and State Government, policymakers, statistical practitioners, academicians, and representatives from national and international organizations. Beyond commemorating its foundation, the occasion serves as a platform to reflect on NSSTA’s journey and to chart the way forward in strengthening India’s statistical capacity to face emerging challenges. **** Samrat/ (Release ID: 2226485) Visitor Counter : 191 Read this release in: हिन्दी Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation National Statistical Systems Training Academy, MoSPI to Celebrate 18th Foundation Day on 13th February 2026 Theme: Reimagining Capacity Building for Official Statistics to achieve vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 Posted On:

title: UPSC to Open Three-Day “Correction Window” as a One Time Measure for Civil Services Examination & Indian Forest Service Examination, 2026
content:
Press Release:Press Information Bureau UPSC UPSC to Open Three-Day “Correction Window” as a One Time Measure for Civil Services Examination & Indian Forest Service Examination, 2026 Posted On:
                11 FEB 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is planning to open a three-day “Correction Window” as a one-time measure for aspirants/candidates to rectify mistakes in the application forms submitted for the Civil Services Examination (CSE), 2026 and Indian Forest Service (IFoS) Examination, 2026. The Correction Window will provide candidates an opportunity to edit their details and make necessary corrections in the Common Application Form and the Examination Application Form, as applicable. A similar correction facility had also been provided last year for candidates of the NDA & NA Examination (II), 2025 and the CDS Examination (II), 2025. The UPSC Online Application Portal consists of four parts, arranged in separate cards on the home page. Three of these - Account Creation, Universal Registration and Common Application Form - contain information common to all examinations and can be filled at any time by candidates. The fourth part, i.e. Examinations, is the examination specific module and contains examination notices, the Examination Application and application status. Speaking about the “correction window”, UPSC Chairman Dr. Ajay Kumar said, “The Commission remains committed to making the application process more accessible, transparent and candidate-friendly. While the portal incorporates multiple checks before final submission, a limited correction facility is being provided as a one-time measure to ensure integrity of the application process and address genuine concerns of applicants.” The three-day Correction Window will open after the closing of the online application process. Detailed instructions regarding the exact dates and scope of permissible corrections will be notified on the Commission’s website in due course. The new Online Application Portal was launched on 28 May 2025, replacing the earlier One Time Registration (OTR) module. Applications for Civil Services Examination, 2026 and Indian Forest Service Examination, 2026 are being accepted through this portal. **** AK/SK (Release ID: 2226481) Visitor Counter : 181 Read this release in: हिन्दी UPSC UPSC to Open Three-Day “Correction Window” as a One Time Measure for Civil Services Examination & Indian Forest Service Examination, 2026 Posted On:
